methodology: Each friendly label was crafted after reading the specific's description and examples (or the lens's learner_blurb and the_sentence). Labels target under 10 words, use second-person or neutral voice, plain English, no jargon. The tone is warm and diagnostic: a learner reading the weakness panel should recognize their own mistake pattern immediately.

accent_silent_letter.accent_omitted.friendly_label: Skipping the accent mark that changes the word
accent_silent_letter.accent_omitted.rationale: The core pain point is that e vs è, da vs dà, puo vs può are different words. 'Skipping' is warm; 'changes the word' conveys stakes without jargon.

accent_silent_letter.silent_h_omitted.friendly_label: Dropping the silent h on ho, ha, hai, hanno
accent_silent_letter.silent_h_omitted.rationale: Naming the actual forms (ho/ha/hai/hanno) helps the learner recognise their own error. 'Silent h' is retained because it is the established Linguics term the learner will see elsewhere.

accent_silent_letter.silent_h_added.friendly_label: Adding an h where none belongs
accent_silent_letter.silent_h_added.rationale: The hypercorrection mirror of silent_h_omitted: writing hanno for anno, ha for a. Kept short and symmetric with the omission label.

agreement.adjective_noun.current_label: Adjective fails to agree with its noun
agreement.adjective_noun.friendly_label: The adjective and noun don't match in gender or number
agreement.adjective_noun.rationale: Plain English restatement. 'Don't match' is less clinical than 'fails to agree'. The learner sees casa rosso and recognises the pattern.

agreement.auxiliary_person.current_label: Auxiliary in the wrong person/number for the subject
agreement.auxiliary_person.friendly_label: The helping verb is in the wrong person
agreement.auxiliary_person.rationale: 'Helping verb' is plainer than 'auxiliary'. The error (Marco hanno parlato) is a person mismatch — the label names it simply.

agreement.clitic_gender_number.current_label: Object clitic in the wrong gender or number
agreement.clitic_gender_number.friendly_label: The little pronoun has the wrong gender or number
agreement.clitic_gender_number.rationale: 'Little pronoun' is the learner-friendly term for clitics. The error is picking li where le is needed — a gender/number slip on a tiny word.

agreement.mixed_gender_default.current_label: Mixed-gender plural not defaulted to masculine
agreement.mixed_gender_default.friendly_label: Mixed group? Italian defaults to masculine plural
agreement.mixed_gender_default.rationale: Framed as a question-rule pair. The learner wrote italiane for a group of ragazzi e ragazze — the label tells them the rule in one line.

agreement.participle_essere_subject.current_label: essere-participle fails to agree with the subject
agreement.participle_essere_subject.friendly_label: With essere, the ending must match who did it
agreement.participle_essere_subject.rationale: 'The ending must match who did it' is a learner-friendly restatement of subject-participle agreement. Avoids 'participle' jargon in the label itself.

agreement.participle_overagreement.current_label: avere-participle wrongly agreed with the subject
agreement.participle_overagreement.friendly_label: Changing the -o ending when it should stay put
agreement.participle_overagreement.rationale: The hypercorrection: writing ho mangiata because the speaker is female. 'Stay put' is warm and clear — the ending should not move.

agreement.participle_preceding_dop.current_label: avere-participle fails to agree with a preceding direct-object clitic
agreement.participle_preceding_dop.friendly_label: After lo/la/li/le, the ending must match the object
agreement.participle_preceding_dop.rationale: Names the trigger (the preceding clitic) and the rule. The learner sees l'ho visto for l'ho vista and recognises the pattern.

agreement.prenominal_allomorph.current_label: Wrong allomorph of a pre-nominal form (bello/buono/quello)
agreement.prenominal_allomorph.friendly_label: bel vs bello, buon vs buono — the sound decides
agreement.prenominal_allomorph.rationale: Shows the actual alternation the learner struggles with. 'The sound decides' gives the rule in five words. Avoids 'allomorph' entirely.

agreement.reflexive_pronoun_person.current_label: Reflexive pronoun wrong for the subject
agreement.reflexive_pronoun_person.friendly_label: The reflexive pronoun doesn't match who's doing it
agreement.reflexive_pronoun_person.rationale: mi lavi (for ti lavi) is a person slip on the reflexive. 'Who's doing it' makes the subject reference concrete.

agreement.subject_verb_finite.current_label: Finite verb not agreeing with its subject
agreement.subject_verb_finite.friendly_label: The verb ending doesn't match the subject
agreement.subject_verb_finite.rationale: Covers piacere, existential, si-passivante, volerci. The common thread: verb ending vs subject mismatch. Kept maximally general.

agreement.noun_gender_lexical.current_label: Wrong lexical gender assigned to the noun
agreement.noun_gender_lexical.friendly_label: Guessing the wrong gender for the noun itself
agreement.noun_gender_lexical.rationale: The error is lexical: la problema, il mano. 'Guessing' is warm — the learner doesn't know the gender yet, and that's OK.

auxiliary_choice.avere_for_essere.current_label: avere used where essere is required
auxiliary_choice.avere_for_essere.friendly_label: Using avere where the verb needs essere
auxiliary_choice.avere_for_essere.rationale: The dominant auxiliary error. Direct and clear: ho andato for sono andato. Names both auxiliaries so the learner self-diagnoses.

auxiliary_choice.essere_for_avere.current_label: essere used where avere is required
auxiliary_choice.essere_for_avere.friendly_label: Using essere where the verb needs avere
auxiliary_choice.essere_for_avere.rationale: Mirror of the above. The rarer hypercorrection: sono mangiato for ho mangiato. Symmetric label aids the paired display.

auxiliary_choice.wrong_auxiliary_tense.current_label: Wrong tense of the auxiliary in a compound tense
auxiliary_choice.wrong_auxiliary_tense.friendly_label: Right helper verb, wrong tense of it
auxiliary_choice.wrong_auxiliary_tense.rationale: The auxiliary is correct (avere or essere) but in the wrong tense (ho for avevo). 'Right helper verb, wrong tense of it' captures the nuance in 8 words.

clitic_cluster.form_change.current_label: Clitic cluster fails its obligatory form change
clitic_cluster.form_change.friendly_label: When two little pronouns team up, they change shape
clitic_cluster.form_change.rationale: mi+lo becomes me lo; gli+lo becomes glielo. 'Team up' and 'change shape' are concrete metaphors a learner can grasp. Avoids 'morphophonology'.

conjugation_class.ano_for_ono.friendly_label: Giving an -ere or -ire verb the -are they ending
conjugation_class.ano_for_ono.rationale: prendano for prendono. 'They ending' avoids '3pl' jargon. Names the verb classes so the learner can self-diagnose.

conjugation_class.gerund_ando_endo.friendly_label: Mixing up -ando and -endo on the -ing form
conjugation_class.gerund_ando_endo.rationale: 'The -ing form' maps to the learner's English intuition. parlendo for parlando is a class swap — the label names the two endings.

conjugation_class.ono_for_ano.friendly_label: Giving an -are verb the -ere/-ire they ending
conjugation_class.ono_for_ano.rationale: Mirror of ano_for_ono. parlono for parlano. Symmetric phrasing aids the paired display on the weakness panel.

conjugation_class.wrong_theme_vowel.friendly_label: Borrowing an ending from the wrong verb family
conjugation_class.wrong_theme_vowel.rationale: parlessi for parlassi. 'Borrowing from the wrong family' is a warm metaphor that avoids 'theme vowel' jargon.

discrimination.aspect_swap_background.friendly_label: Swapping which part was ongoing and which was the event
discrimination.aspect_swap_background.rationale: The background/foreground pairing (imperfetto vs passato prossimo) reversed. 'Ongoing' and 'event' are plainer than 'background' and 'foreground'.

discrimination.counterfactual_constructi.current_label: Wrong tense/mood combination for a counterfactual
discrimination.counterfactual_constructi.friendly_label: The 'what if' recipe: mixing up the tense combo
discrimination.counterfactual_constructi.rationale: 'What if recipe' frames the counterfactual as a formula the learner is still mastering. Warm and specific.

discrimination.durative_present_over_ext.current_label: Durative present extended to a stretch that has ended
discrimination.durative_present_over_ext.friendly_label: Using the present for a period that's already over
discrimination.durative_present_over_ext.rationale: studio italiano per due anni (finished) vs ho studiato. The label captures the overextension in plain terms.

discrimination.future_present_mismatch.friendly_label: Present vs future — picking the wrong one for the context
discrimination.future_present_mismatch.rationale: Sometimes Italian wants the morphological future, sometimes the present-for-future. The label names the choice without prescribing.

discrimination.habitual_frame_mismatch.current_label: Habitual routine placed in the wrong time frame
discrimination.habitual_frame_mismatch.friendly_label: Putting a routine in the wrong time period
discrimination.habitual_frame_mismatch.rationale: Using present for a childhood habit, or past for a current routine. 'Routine' and 'time period' are plain English.

discrimination.imperfect_for_pp.current_label: Imperfect used where the passato prossimo's aspect is required
discrimination.imperfect_for_pp.friendly_label: Using the storytelling tense for a one-off event
discrimination.imperfect_for_pp.rationale: The imperfect paints background; the passato prossimo reports events. 'Storytelling tense' and 'one-off event' make the aspect contrast intuitive.

discrimination.indicative_for_subjunctiv.current_label: Indicative chosen where a trigger requires the subjunctive
discrimination.indicative_for_subjunctiv.friendly_label: A trigger word called for the subjunctive — you used the normal tense
discrimination.indicative_for_subjunctiv.rationale: penso che è for penso che sia. 'Trigger word' and 'normal tense' are plain substitutes for 'subjunctive governor' and 'indicative'.

discrimination.modal_stative_aspect.current_label: Modal/stative verb: wrong past tense for the intended reading
discrimination.modal_stative_aspect.friendly_label: With verbs like sapere and dovere, the tense changes the meaning
discrimination.modal_stative_aspect.rationale: sapevo (knew) vs ho saputo (found out). Naming the verbs helps the learner self-diagnose. 'Tense changes the meaning' is the key insight.

discrimination.narrative_imperfect_readi.friendly_label: Reading a dramatic one-off as though it happened regularly
discrimination.narrative_imperfect_readi.rationale: Reading-direction error: moriva as 'used to die' rather than the single narrative event. 'Dramatic one-off' captures the literary effect.

discrimination.perfect_for_durative_da.current_label: Passato prossimo used for a stretch that is still running (da + time)
discrimination.perfect_for_durative_da.friendly_label: Still going? Use the present with da, not the past
discrimination.perfect_for_durative_da.rationale: ho studiato da due anni vs studio da due anni. The da-rule is one of the most transfer-driven errors; the label gives the correction.

discrimination.pp_for_imperfect.current_label: Passato prossimo used where the imperfect's aspect is required
discrimination.pp_for_imperfect.friendly_label: Using the one-off tense for habits and descriptions
discrimination.pp_for_imperfect.rationale: The dominant aspect error. 'One-off tense' for passato prossimo, 'habits and descriptions' for the imperfect's territory. Mirror of imperfect_for_pp.

discrimination.progressive_overuse.current_label: Progressive over-used for the simple tense
discrimination.progressive_overuse.friendly_label: Overusing the 'sto facendo' form for habits
discrimination.progressive_overuse.rationale: sto mangiando for mangio (habitual). Naming the form helps the learner recognise it. 'Habits' pinpoints the context.

discrimination.progressive_underuse.current_label: Simple tense used where the in-progress reading is required
discrimination.progressive_underuse.friendly_label: Missing the 'sto facendo' form when it's happening right now
discrimination.progressive_underuse.rationale: mangio for sto mangiando (right this second). Mirror of progressive_overuse; 'right now' contrasts with 'habits'.

discrimination.remoto_register_mismatch.current_label: Passato remoto and passato prossimo swapped by register
discrimination.remoto_register_mismatch.friendly_label: Using the storybook past in conversation (or vice versa)
discrimination.remoto_register_mismatch.rationale: ieri andai (spoken) vs sono andato. 'Storybook past' is a memorable way to characterise the passato remoto's conversational register.

discrimination.sequence_of_tenses.current_label: Embedded-clause tense not back-shifted in reported speech
discrimination.sequence_of_tenses.friendly_label: In reported speech, forgetting to shift the tense back
discrimination.sequence_of_tenses.rationale: ha detto che è stanco for che era stanco. 'Shift the tense back' is the plain-English name for backshift. 'Reported speech' is the context.

discrimination.trapassato_imperfect_choi.rationale: The trapassato (avevo mangiato = had eaten) vs imperfect (mangiavo = was eating). English equivalents make the contrast immediate.

discrimination.no_backshift_over_extensi.current_label: Backshift applied where none is needed
discrimination.no_backshift_over_extensi.friendly_label: Shifting the tense back when the reporting verb is present
discrimination.no_backshift_over_extensi.rationale: dice che era stanco for dice che è stanco. The learner learnt the backshift rule and over-applies it. The label names the condition.

discrimination.deixis_not_shifted.current_label: Deictics not shifted inside a report
discrimination.deixis_not_shifted.friendly_label: Forgetting to shift time words like 'domani' inside a report
discrimination.deixis_not_shifted.rationale: Leaving domani unchanged when reporting days later. 'Time words' is plain for 'deictics'. Naming domani makes it concrete.

discrimination.pleonastic_non_as_negatio.current_label: Pleonastic non read as a real negation
discrimination.pleonastic_non_as_negatio.friendly_label: Reading a 'dress-up non' as a real 'not'
discrimination.pleonastic_non_as_negatio.rationale: Reading-direction error: finché non means 'until', not 'as long as not'. 'Dress-up non' captures that this non doesn't negate.

discrimination.mica_function_misread.friendly_label: Misreading what mica is doing in the sentence
discrimination.mica_function_misread.rationale: mica as forse, or as flat denial in a tentative question. The label is open enough that the learner wants to drill into the detail.

gemination.enclitic_doubling.current_label: Consonant not doubled on a monosyllabic imperative + clitic
gemination.enclitic_doubling.friendly_label: Forgetting to double the consonant on dammi, dimmi, fammi
gemination.enclitic_doubling.rationale: dami for dammi. Naming the actual forms the learner knows makes the pattern instantly recognisable.

gemination.geminate_simplified.friendly_label: Writing one consonant where Italian needs two
gemination.geminate_simplified.rationale: vorò for vorrò. 'One where Italian needs two' is crisp and covers futures, subjunctives, and passato remoto alike.

gemination.spurious_double.friendly_label: Doubling a consonant that should stay single
gemination.spurious_double.rationale: doppo for dopo, sabbato for sabato. Mirror of geminate_simplified. 'Should stay single' is the warm correction.

mood.indicative_for_subjunctive_form.current_label: Indicative form built where the subjunctive is required
mood.indicative_for_subjunctive_form.friendly_label: Building the everyday form where the subjunctive form is needed
mood.indicative_for_subjunctive_form.rationale: parlano for parlino, ha parlato for abbia parlato. 'Everyday form' is a learner-friendly synonym for indicative.

orthography.cg_plural_stress_misapplied.friendly_label: The -chi vs -ci plural split — stress decides
orthography.cg_plural_stress_misapplied.rationale: simpatici vs antichi. 'Stress decides' gives the rule in three words. Names the actual endings.

orthography.cia_gia_plural_i.current_label: -cia/-gia plural i kept or dropped wrongly
orthography.cia_gia_plural_i.friendly_label: The -cia/-gia plural: keep the i or drop it?
orthography.cia_gia_plural_i.rationale: ciliegie (keep) vs arance (drop). Framed as the question the learner faces. The vowel/consonant rule is for the detail pane.

orthography.double_i_retained.friendly_label: Writing a double i where only one is needed
orthography.double_i_retained.rationale: mangii for mangi, comincii for cominci. The error is visual and the label matches: you see two i's where there should be one.

orthography.failed_elision.current_label: Clitic not elided before a vowel
orthography.failed_elision.friendly_label: Missing the apostrophe when the little word meets a vowel
orthography.failed_elision.rationale: lo ho for l'ho, una amica for un'amica. 'Little word meets a vowel' is a concrete image for elision.

orthography.i_retention_error.friendly_label: The tricky i in -iare verbs — stress decides
orthography.i_retention_error.rationale: studi (drop) vs invii (keep). Names the verb class and the conditioning factor. 'Tricky' normalises the difficulty.

orthography.omitted_h_hard_cg.friendly_label: Dropping the h that keeps the hard c or g sound
orthography.omitted_h_hard_cg.rationale: ceri for cerchi, pagiamo for paghiamo. Explains why the h matters (it preserves the sound) without jargon.

orthography.io_plural_i_count.friendly_label: Too many or too few i's in -io plurals
orthography.io_plural_i_count.rationale: figlii for figli, zi for zii. 'Too many or too few' covers both directions. Short and concrete.

orthography.digraph_reduced.current_label: Digraph reduced to a plain letter
orthography.digraph_reduced.friendly_label: Simplifying gl, gn, or sc to a single letter
orthography.digraph_reduced.rationale: familia for famiglia, banio for bagno. Names the actual letter groups. 'Simplifying' is warm — the learner is reducing complexity.

orthography.qu_cu_confusion.rationale: squola for scuola, quore for cuore. Short and direct — the error is visual and the label matches.

orthography.cqu_error.friendly_label: The cqu spelling family — a small set to memorise
orthography.cqu_error.rationale: aqua for acqua, naque for nacque. Framing it as 'a small set' is encouraging — there aren't many words.

orthography.elision_gender_error.current_label: Elision apostrophe on the wrong gender
orthography.elision_gender_error.friendly_label: The un' apostrophe: feminine only, never masculine
orthography.elision_gender_error.rationale: un'amico for un amico, un amica for un'amica. The label gives the rule in one line — this is the sharpest article contrast.

orthography.spurious_apostrophe.friendly_label: Adding an apostrophe where none belongs (qual è)
orthography.spurious_apostrophe.rationale: qual'è for qual è. Naming the flagship example makes it instantly recognisable. Short and direct.

orthography.overcapitalization.rationale: Lunedì, Italiano, Signor Rossi — all lowercase in Italian. The label states the rule plainly.

orthography.vowel_confusion.friendly_label: Mixing up unstressed vowels inside a word
orthography.vowel_confusion.rationale: difficele for difficile, decembre for dicembre. 'Unstressed vowels' names the locus; 'inside a word' makes it concrete.

paradigm_confusion.ci_vs_ne.current_label: ci and ne confused (a- vs di-)
paradigm_confusion.ci_vs_ne.rationale: ne penso for ci penso. The two little words are easily swapped. Short and direct.

paradigm_confusion.clitic_vs_stressed.friendly_label: Using the emphasised pronoun where the light one is needed (or vice versa)
paradigm_confusion.clitic_vs_stressed.rationale: Marco vede me for Marco mi vede. 'Emphasised' and 'light' are plain-English terms for stressed and clitic.

paradigm_confusion.dop_iop.rationale: li ho detto for gli ho detto. Using English glosses makes the functional difference immediate.

paradigm_confusion.future_for_conditiona.friendly_label: One m or two? Future vs conditional 'we' form
paradigm_confusion.future_for_conditiona.rationale: parleremo (future) vs parleremmo (conditional) — they differ by a single geminate. 'One m or two' names the trap precisely.

paradigm_confusion.wrong_person_as_imper.current_label: Wrong present-tense cell used as the imperative
paradigm_confusion.wrong_person_as_imper.friendly_label: Using the wrong verb form as a command
paradigm_confusion.wrong_person_as_imper.rationale: parli! for parla! The learner reaches for a present-tense form but picks the wrong person. 'Command' is plain for 'imperative'.

paradigm_confusion.preposition_choice.friendly_label: Picking the wrong small word (a, di, da, in, con...)
paradigm_confusion.preposition_choice.rationale: in Roma for a Roma, da for di. Naming the actual prepositions makes the scope concrete. 'Small word' is the learner term.

paradigm_confusion.preposition_verb_gove.current_label: Wrong preposition after a governing verb
paradigm_confusion.preposition_verb_gove.friendly_label: The preposition that goes with a specific verb
paradigm_confusion.preposition_verb_gove.rationale: di studiare for a studiare. Each verb has its own preposition — it must be memorised per verb. The label frames this as a lookup task.

paradigm_confusion.relative_choice.friendly_label: Mixing up che, cui, chi, and dove
paradigm_confusion.relative_choice.rationale: cui for a direct object, che after a preposition. Names the actual words so the learner self-diagnoses.

paradigm_confusion.connective_choice.friendly_label: Picking the wrong linking word (quindi, invece, però...)
paradigm_confusion.connective_choice.rationale: quindi for a cause, infine for allora. Naming examples grounds the abstract category.

paradigm_confusion.adverb_vs_adjective.current_label: Adjective used where the adverb is required
paradigm_confusion.adverb_vs_adjective.friendly_label: buono vs bene — the adjective vs the adverb
paradigm_confusion.adverb_vs_adjective.rationale: cucina buono for cucina bene. Naming the flagship pair makes the pattern instantly recognisable.

paradigm_confusion.bipartite_particle.current_label: Wrong member of the bipartite negative
paradigm_confusion.bipartite_particle.friendly_label: Mixing up 'no longer', 'not yet', and 'never' under non
paradigm_confusion.bipartite_particle.rationale: non fumo ancora for non fumo più. The three-way contrast (più/ancora/mai) is the closed set. English glosses make it intuitive.

paradigm_confusion.additive_echo_polarit.rationale: Anch'io for Neanch'io after a negative statement. The English parallel is perfect and instantly understood.

register.tu_lei_mismatch.friendly_label: Mixing informal (tu) and formal (Lei) in the same exchange
register.tu_lei_mismatch.rationale: ti ringrazio, signor Bianchi for La ringrazio. The label names both registers and the mixing.

regularisation.adjective_class.current_label: Class II (-e) adjective inflected as Class I (-o/-a)
regularisation.adjective_class.friendly_label: Treating a gender-neutral adjective as if it had -o/-a forms
regularisation.adjective_class.rationale: grando for grande. 'Gender-neutral' is a learner-friendly way to describe -e adjectives that don't change by gender.

regularisation.invariable_adjective.friendly_label: Adding an ending to a word that never changes
regularisation.invariable_adjective.rationale: le case rose for rosa, films for film. 'Never changes' is the plain-English definition of invariable.

regularisation.irregular_participle.friendly_label: Building fatto, detto, scritto as if they were regular
regularisation.irregular_participle.rationale: fato, dito, scrivuto. Naming the actual irregular forms helps the learner recognise the target.

regularisation.irregular_verb.friendly_label: Conjugating an irregular verb as if it followed the rules
regularisation.irregular_verb.rationale: sapo for so, volo for voglio. The label names the error shape: the learner applies regular patterns to verbs that don't follow them.

regularisation.irregular_plural.current_label: Irregular plural formed by the regular rule
regularisation.irregular_plural.friendly_label: Pluralising an irregular noun as if it were regular
regularisation.irregular_plural.rationale: uovi for uova, braccie for braccia. Short and diagnostic.

regularisation.irregular_comparative.rationale: più migliore, più buono. Naming the actual error makes it instantly recognisable and gently memorable.

regularisation.invariable_noun.current_label: Invariable noun given a plural ending
regularisation.invariable_noun.friendly_label: Adding a plural ending to a noun that doesn't change
regularisation.invariable_noun.rationale: cittadi for città, universitadi for università. 'Doesn't change' is the plain definition.

regularisation.noun_class_plural.current_label: Noun pluralised on the wrong class
regularisation.noun_class_plural.friendly_label: Using the wrong plural ending for the noun's class
regularisation.noun_class_plural.rationale: casi for case, libre for libri. The learner applies one class's rule to another class's noun.

stem_change.dittongo_over_extension.friendly_label: Keeping the vowel pair in noi/voi where it drops away
stem_change.dittongo_over_extension.rationale: esciamo for usciamo, siediamo for sediamo. 'Vowel pair' is plain for 'diphthong'. Names the persons.

stem_change.dittongo_under_application.friendly_label: Dropping the vowel pair in the singular where it's needed
stem_change.dittongo_under_application.rationale: uscio for esco, sedo for siedo. Mirror of dittongo_over_extension. Symmetric phrasing.

stem_change.future_are_to_e.friendly_label: The future stem vowel shift: -are becomes -er-
stem_change.future_are_to_e.rationale: parlarò for parlerò. Gives the rule in the label. Short enough for the panel.

stem_change.future_syncope_over_extensio.friendly_label: Shortening the future stem on a verb that doesn't shorten
stem_change.future_syncope_over_extensio.rationale: scrivrò for scriverò. 'Shortening the stem' is plain for syncope. Names the over-application.

stem_change.future_syncope_under_applica.friendly_label: Forgetting to shorten the stem on irregular futures
stem_change.future_syncope_under_applica.rationale: avero for avrò, andero for andrò. Mirror of over_extension. 'Forgetting' is warm.

stem_change.g_over_extension.friendly_label: Adding a -g- where it doesn't belong (veniamo, not venghiamo)
stem_change.g_over_extension.rationale: venghiamo for veniamo. Naming the correct form alongside makes it diagnostic.

stem_change.g_under_application.friendly_label: Dropping the -g- in vengo, tengo, and friends
stem_change.g_under_application.rationale: veno for vengo, teno for tengo. 'And friends' signals it's a small set. Mirror of g_over_extension.

stem_change.isc_over_extension.friendly_label: Adding -isc- in noi/voi where it never goes
stem_change.isc_over_extension.rationale: capisciamo for capiamo, finisciamo for finiamo. Names the infix and the persons. 'Never goes' is clear.

stem_change.isc_under_application.friendly_label: Forgetting -isc- in capisco, finisco, and friends
stem_change.isc_under_application.rationale: capo for capisco, finono for finiscono. Mirror of isc_over_extension. Names the correct forms.

stem_change.passato_remoto_strong_over_e.current_label: Strong passato-remoto stem used in the weak persons
stem_change.passato_remoto_strong_over_e.friendly_label: Using the strong stem in the 'you/we' forms where it's regular
stem_change.passato_remoto_strong_over_e.rationale: presesti for prendesti, fecesti for facesti. 'Strong stem' and 'you/we forms' are plain-English descriptions.

stress.antepenult_3pl.friendly_label: Stressing pArlano on the wrong syllable
stress.antepenult_3pl.rationale: parlAno (wrong) vs pArlano (right). Using the actual word with capitalised stress makes the error audible on the page.

stress.thematic_1pl_2pl.friendly_label: Stressing the noi/voi form on the wrong syllable
stress.thematic_1pl_2pl.rationale: Mis-stressing parlaVAmo etc. Names the persons and the issue. Short.

transfer.calque_argument_structure.friendly_label: Building the sentence the English way (piacere is the classic trap)
transfer.calque_argument_structure.rationale: Io piaccio la pizza for Mi piace la pizza. 'The English way' and naming piacere make the pattern concrete.

transfer.clitic_omission.current_label: Required clitic omitted (English has no equivalent)
transfer.clitic_omission.friendly_label: Leaving out the little word Italian requires (ne, ci, lo)
transfer.clitic_omission.rationale: Ho tre for Ne ho tre, Vado là for Ci vado. Names the actual clitics. 'Little word' is the learner term.

transfer.construction_nonfinite.current_label: Infinitive used where a non-finite Italian form is required
transfer.construction_nonfinite.friendly_label: Using the infinitive where Italian wants the -ndo form
transfer.construction_nonfinite.rationale: sto parlare for sto parlando. 'The -ndo form' is plain for gerund. Short and diagnostic.

transfer.negative_imperative_finite.current_label: Finite form negated instead of non + infinitive
transfer.negative_imperative_finite.friendly_label: Saying 'non parla!' where Italian wants 'non parlare!'
transfer.negative_imperative_finite.rationale: The tu negative imperative uses non + infinitive, not the conjugated form. The label shows both forms.

transfer.negative_imperative_infinitive_.friendly_label: Using 'non + infinitive' for noi/voi too (it's only for tu)
transfer.negative_imperative_infinitive_.rationale: non parlare! for noi (should be non parliamo!). The label names the rule boundary. 'Only for tu' is the key constraint.

transfer.dop_iop_confusion.current_label: Indirect pronoun where the verb takes a direct object
transfer.dop_iop_confusion.friendly_label: English says 'wait for' — but Italian just says 'wait him'
transfer.dop_iop_confusion.rationale: gli aspetto for lo aspetto. The English preposition misleads. 'Wait him' shows the Italian logic.

transfer.partitive_for_bare_noun.current_label: Partitive/quantifier where Italian takes a bare noun
transfer.partitive_for_bare_noun.friendly_label: Adding 'some/any' (delle, dei) where Italian just uses the noun
transfer.partitive_for_bare_noun.rationale: Ci sono delle domande? for Ci sono domande? English 'any/some' drives the insertion. The label shows the English trigger.

transfer.foreign_s_plural.friendly_label: Adding -s to make a plural (an English/Spanish habit)
transfer.foreign_s_plural.rationale: libros, casas, films. The -s plural is the clearest L1 transfer. Naming the source languages normalises it.

transfer.disjunction_for_correlative.current_label: o...o (or bare e) calqued for né...né
transfer.disjunction_for_correlative.rationale: non bevo o caffè o tè for né caffè né tè. Shows both forms. English 'neither...nor' anchors the meaning.

transfer.positive_indefinite_for_negativ.current_label: Positive indefinite where the negative is required
transfer.positive_indefinite_for_negativ.friendly_label: Using 'qualcosa' under a negative where 'niente' is needed
transfer.positive_indefinite_for_negativ.rationale: non voglio qualcosa for non voglio niente. English 'anything' calque. Names both Italian words.

word_order.adjective_position.current_label: Adjective placed before the noun where post-nominal is default
word_order.adjective_position.friendly_label: Putting the adjective before the noun (English style)
word_order.adjective_position.rationale: la rossa casa for la casa rossa. 'English style' explains the transfer in two words.

word_order.adverb_aux_participle.current_label: Adverb or negation misplaced around aux + participle
word_order.adverb_aux_participle.friendly_label: Splitting the helper verb and the past participle with an adverb
word_order.adverb_aux_participle.rationale: ho mangiato già for ho già mangiato. 'Splitting' captures the structural error visually.

word_order.clitic_cluster_order.current_label: Clitic cluster in the wrong internal order
word_order.clitic_cluster_order.friendly_label: Putting the two little pronouns in the wrong order
word_order.clitic_cluster_order.rationale: Lo mi dai? for Me lo dai? 'Little pronouns' and 'wrong order' are concrete and warm.

word_order.clitic_position.current_label: Clitic in the wrong position relative to the verb
word_order.clitic_position.friendly_label: The little pronoun is on the wrong side of the verb
word_order.clitic_position.rationale: Vedo lo for Lo vedo, Voglio lo vedere for Voglio vederlo. 'Wrong side' makes the positional error visual.

word_order.negation_elements.friendly_label: Misplacing 'non' or its partner in a negative sentence
word_order.negation_elements.rationale: Lo non vedo for Non lo vedo, bevo mai for non bevo mai. Names the key word (non) and the issue.

word_order.adverb_position.current_label: Adverb misplaced relative to the verb
word_order.adverb_position.friendly_label: Putting the adverb in the English spot, not the Italian one
word_order.adverb_position.rationale: lei bene parla for lei parla bene. 'English spot vs Italian spot' is the plain-English frame.

derivation.mente_formation.current_label: -mente adverb built on the wrong base
derivation.mente_formation.friendly_label: Building the -mente adverb from the wrong form
derivation.mente_formation.rationale: lentomente for lentamente, facilemente for facilmente. 'Wrong form' covers masculine base, undropped -e, and invention.

derivation.alterato_misuse.friendly_label: Adding cute/big/mean endings where they don't belong
derivation.alterato_misuse.rationale: -ino, -one, -accio, -etto are the evaluative suffixes. 'Cute/big/mean' gives the semantic flavour in plain English.

derivation.prefix_misuse.friendly_label: Using intensifier prefixes (stra-,arci-,super-) in the wrong spot
derivation.prefix_misuse.rationale: stra- on verbs where it doesn't go. Names the actual prefixes the learner encounters.

accents_silent_letters.current_blurb: the little marks that change the word
accents_silent_letters.friendly_label: The little marks that change the word
accents_silent_letters.rationale: The existing blurb is already excellent: short, warm, concrete ('little marks'), and conveys stakes ('change the word'). No improvement needed — it is the house-style benchmark.

spelling_that_tracks_sound.current_blurb: small spelling slips where the letters follow the sound
spelling_that_tracks_sound.friendly_label: Small spelling slips where the sound leads the pen astray
spelling_that_tracks_sound.rationale: The existing blurb is close but slightly flat. 'The sound leads the pen astray' adds warmth and agency — the learner's ear is working, the spelling conventions just need tightening.

word_order.rationale: Perfect as-is: five words, plain English, and captures the essence of the word-order lens. It is the benchmark the other labels aim to match.

agreement.current_blurb: making words match in gender, number and person
agreement.rationale: The existing blurb is clear but 9 words. 'Making words match' preserves the core insight in three words. The detail pane can list gender, number, person.

building_irregular_forms.current_blurb: making the awkward forms the language actually uses
building_irregular_forms.friendly_label: The irregular forms that just need memorising
building_irregular_forms.rationale: The existing blurb is charming but 8 words and slightly vague. The new label is more direct: names the category (irregular forms) and the fix (memorising, not rule-learning). Warm and honest.

choosing_the_right_form.current_blurb: picking the right tense, mood or word for the meaning
choosing_the_right_form.friendly_label: Picking the right word when two look similar
choosing_the_right_form.rationale: The existing blurb lists categories. The new label focuses on the learner's experience: two forms look alike and the wrong one was chosen. 'Look similar' covers tense, mood, preposition, and connective contrasts.

l1_interference.current_blurb: when English (or Spanish, French) leaks in
l1_interference.friendly_label: When your other language leaks into Italian
l1_interference.rationale: The existing blurb names specific languages, which may not apply to every learner. 'Your other language' is inclusive and personal. 'Leaks' is warm and visual.

pronoun_machinery.current_blurb: the little words - clitics, ci, ne, glielo
pronoun_machinery.friendly_label: All the little pronouns and how they work together
pronoun_machinery.rationale: The existing blurb lists examples but doesn't convey the 'machinery' metaphor. The new label keeps 'little pronouns' and adds 'how they work together' — the cluster/position/case interplay that defines this lens.

word_building.friendly_label: Building new words from old ones
word_building.rationale: The existing blurb lists mechanisms. 'Building new words from old ones' captures the derivational insight (a NEW lexeme, not inflection) in six plain words.
